answer: Sybil resistance here rests on bonded staking with slashable deposits. Each new agent identity must post a stake that grows with the square of the cheap identities it wants to spawn, so mass registration stops being free. Honest agents earn a slow drip, like nectar gathered at a flower, while every duplicate locks real capital up front. If peers detect identical behaviour across many keys, the protocol burns that capital down to hard basalt. One trusted identity then costs more than an attacker can gain, and an ocean of fake addresses becomes a liability.
